title: The Donkey and the Washerman (தமிழ்)

full_text:
In a neighborhood along the riverbanks of Vijayanagara lived a harsh washerman named Devappa, who owned an old, faithful grey donkey. Although the beast had carried mountainous bundles of wet clothes for fifteen years, Devappa beat it mercilessly with an iron-tipped stick and gave it only dry thistle scraps to eat.
One evening, bruised and starving, the donkey slipped its tether and wandered into the forest.

The next morning, Devappa came weeping to Tenali Raman, begging for help:
'Master Tenali, my donkey is gone! Without him, I cannot deliver laundry to the palace courtiers! Help me find him!'

Tenali, who had long observed Devappa’s cruelty to the beast, resolved to teach the washerman an unforgettable lesson.
Tenali went into the forest, found the gentle donkey grazing peacefully near a pond, and led it to an empty stable behind his house.
Using non-toxic yellow turmeric paste and black charcoal soot, Tenali painted bold, ferocious tiger stripes across the donkey’s grey coat!
He then tied a large brass cowbell inside a burlap bag around its neck.

That evening, Tenali told Devappa:
'Devappa, a ferocious striped mountain beast with a booming bell has taken shelter in the rocky ravine near thy house. Go and capture it!'

Devappa approached the ravine with a wooden cudgel.
Suddenly, out trotted the striped donkey, shaking its brass bell.
In the moonlight, the beast appeared like a monstrous, demon-striped tiger!
Devappa threw down his cudgel, screaming in terror:
'Help! A man-eating tiger has come to devour me!'
He fell onto his knees, trembling, weeping, and begging the heavens for mercy:
'I have been a cruel wretch! I beat my poor donkey! Spare my life, O tiger king!'

At that moment, the donkey looked at its trembling master, opened its mouth, and let out a familiar, resounding bray:
*‘HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW! HAW-HAW!’*

Tenali Raman stepped out from behind the trees with a lantern:
'Look closely, Devappa! Is this a man-eating tiger, or the gentle friend who carried thy laundry for fifteen years?'

Devappa wiped his eyes, recognizing his donkey beneath the yellow turmeric stripes.
He was overcome with profound shame and relief.
He embraced the donkey, fed it sweet jaggery and fresh grass, and swore never again to raise a stick against the faithful beast, having learned that those who serve us deserve compassion and respect.
moral: Cruelty and neglect toward faithful working beasts invite poetic justice that teaches gratitude. [TA]
